transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-05-06
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration approx: 54 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Evan Chao (CTO, Brighton), Maya Singh (Lead Platform Engineer), Tom Becker (Head of Security), Rhiannon O'Keefe (ML Engineer)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough): Architectural kickoff to map integration points for Redwood serving modes (hosted/dedicated/private), clarify SDK and LangChain/LlamaIndex connector needs, gateway/proxy placement, and instrumentation/observability.

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros and then we'll jump into architecture. I'm Samira (AE), with Diego from solutions. how's everyone doing?
[00:15] Evan: Good, thanks. brief context — Brighton's building an internal assistant and an insights API. We're evaluating options for inference runtime; latency matters for interactive use, also a lot of regulated PII.
[00:28] Diego: Great, can you share what your current stack looks like? are you running LangChain or LlamaIndex at the moment?
[00:34] Maya: yeah, we're on LangChain mostly, with a wrap around for embedding and a LlamaIndex store for retrieval. That said, some teams call models directly through an internal gateway. We have an nginx ingress that funnels traffic, and there's a sidecar pattern for auth.
[00:50] Rhiannon: and for models we skew open weights — quantized delta models — but some subsystems use hosted APIs for RAG since we haven't scaled inference yet.
[01:05] Tom: security note — we need FIPS-ish KMS integration, audit trails, and SOC2 type controls. data can't leave eu-west-1 for certain flows. also we have DLP scanners on ingest.
[01:20] Samira: Understood. Redwood supports hosted, dedicated pools, and private (VPC/on-prem) options. For EU residency we can pin regions and integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping. Diego will walk through the footprint and integration points.
[01:35] Diego: Let's start with the simplest flow: call to Redwood Hosted via our public API. pros: fastest to get started, no infra to manage, stream responses. cons: you hand requests to our hosted tier — we understand residency constraints so you can opt for regional hosting but for strict EU-only, Dedicated or Private is usually chosen.
[01:55] Evan: So we'd likely consider Dedicated or Private for the initial high-sensitivity workloads. Dedicated because predictability of throughput, Private for air-gapped regulated stuff. can you explain how the gateway sits between our ingress and Redwood?
[02:10] Diego: Sure. three main patterns we've seen: 1) direct SDK calls from service -> Redwood SDK (recommended for simplicity), 2) leave a gateway/proxy in front that translates internal traffic to Redwood—useful if you need token routing, rate limiting, or transformation, 3) sidecar pattern where each service hosts a small proxy that manages batching and KV cache locally.
[02:35] Maya: we're using a centralized gateway that enforces RBAC and quota today. we want to avoid reworking a lot. can Redwood's SDK integrate behind our gateway so that calls still surface in our observability? e.g. trace IDs pass-through?
[02:50] Diego: Yes — our SDK supports propagating trace headers (x-request-id, traceparent), and we have observability hooks to emit structured logs and span context. If you use a proxy, it's straightforward to forward those headers. we also support ingesting your tracing into Redwood Console for correlated traces if you onboard dedicated or private and grant read-only access.
[03:10] Tom: On encryption — how do you handle customer-managed keys and HSM?
[03:16] Samira: For Dedicated we offer KMS integration where you manage keys in your cloud KMS; for Private (VPC/on-prem) you can present keys via your HSM/KMS and we can configure the control plane to honor those. We'll share the KMS integration guide.
[03:33] Evan: Good. about SDKs — our workbench is Node + Python. does Redwood have official SDKs and examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex?
[03:42] Diego: We have official SDKs in Python, Node, Java, and Go. for LangChain and LlamaIndex we provide connector examples for both: a LangChain LLM wrapper and a LlamaIndex vector store integration. I'll post code snippets after this call.
[03:58] Rhiannon: any pitfalls with streaming + RAG? we see model tokenization differences and need stable embeddings for our store.
[04:07] Diego: For embeddings consistency we recommend pinning the model family and quantization profile. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and batching profiles based on your prompt distribution. Streaming works fine but you should be careful if your retrieval logic depends on full-response checks; we support chunked streaming with finalization callbacks.
[04:30] Maya: Let's talk rate limits and quotas — our gateway enforces per-tenant quotas and we throttle to keep backend stable. Can Redwood expose per-key quotas we can map to tenants?
[04:42] Samira: Yes, Redwood supports token-based quotas per API key, and rate-limiting policies you can configure. With Dedicated or Private you can define custom quota buckets. You can also attach metadata to requests so we can segment usage by tenant for billing/observability.
[05:00] Evan: How about algorithmic throttling — e.g., we want to prioritize low-latency interactive traffic over batch jobs; can you route by intent?
[05:11] Diego: You can set routing policies at the control plane: route by route tag, by priority header, or by path. For example, route interactive routes to a low-latency dedicated pool and background jobs to a cost-optimized pool with higher batching. We also have automatic fallback to compatible model variants when capacity is constrained.
[05:36] Tom: Observability — what do you emit? traces, token-level cost, per-route latencies?
[05:43] Diego: We emit per-request metadata: latency percentiles, token usage, model variant, and per-token timing for some variants. The Console surfaces token level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and you can hook Prometheus metrics or send logs to your SIEM. For private deployments you can enable longer retention and integrate with your datalake.
[06:05] Maya: Are there prebuilt exporters for Prometheus or OpenTelemetry?
[06:09] Diego: Yes, we provide exporters for Prometheus metrics and an OpenTelemetry collector config snippet. For advanced needs we can export traces to your OTLP endpoint.
[06:20] Evan: Regarding LlamaIndex: our index needs to call embeddings separately and maintain freshness. what's the best pattern? centralize embeddings generation service or let each worker call Redwood?
[06:33] Diego: Tradeoffs: central service simplifies caching and deduping embeddings but can be a bottleneck. Letting each worker call Redwood scales horizontally but watch token costs and duplicate requests. We recommend a middle ground: a shared embedding service with an LRU cache and a batched endpoint to reduce per-token cost. Redwood supports batching and prefix caching; we can also set up a local sidecar that does KV cache for the retrieval augmentation.
[06:58] Rhiannon: For our benchmarks, we need to test p99 latency and throughput for a 1024 token context with retrieval (topK=10). can Redwood run a dedicated pilot in our VPC?
[07:10] Samira: Yes, we can arrange a pilot in Dedicated or Private. For VPC Dedicated we run a control plane handshake and deploy model-serving nodes in your region—should you want complete air-gapped on-prem that's a little longer lead time. We'll need your traffic profile and a list of sample prompts.
[07:29] Maya: about deployment — what's the onboarding time for Dedicated vs Private?
[07:33] Diego: Typical: Dedicated — 2–4 weeks for capacity provisioning and network setup (assuming permissions granted). Private (on-prem) — 6–10 weeks depending on environment and compliance checks. Hosted is immediate.
[07:47] Evan: Cost buckets — what drives price for Dedicated? is it reserved GPU hours or per-token?
[07:53] Samira: Dedicated is primarily a capacity reservation: monthly commit for GPU pools plus per-token or per-inference unit for model usage. We can model pricing for your expected QPS and token distribution and show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[08:08] Tom: On compliance — do you provide audit logs for admin actions and request-level logs for e-discovery?
[08:14] Diego: Yes. For Dedicated and Private we can deliver detailed audit logs, admin action logs, and request metadata with redaction options. Hosted tier provides a more limited retention by default but we have add-ons for extended retention.
[08:29] Maya: Let's get into more technical specifics — network topology. We'll sketch ours: internal gateway -> auth service -> rate-limiter -> routing to internal services. we want Redwood to appear as just another downstream service.
[08:42] Diego: Good. If Redwood is a downstream service you can use the SDK directly in your auth service so that tokens propagate. Alternatively, place Redwood behind your gateway and map tenants to API keys. For KV cache and batching we recommend sidecar on the worker nodes so you can keep cache hot with local access.
[09:03] Evan: Are there constraints on model sizes for Private? we have some huge LLMs that need A100s with specific drivers.
[09:12] Diego: We support a wide range of hardware profiles and can select nodes with driver compatibility. For very large models we may recommend Dedicated pools with validated kernel/driver stacks. We do compatibility testing as part of onboarding.
[09:25] Rhiannon: Can the SDK surface partial tokens for streaming with token-level callbacks?
[09:29] Diego: Yep — both SDKs provide streaming iterators that yield token chunks and provide finalization events. We also have server side event (SSE) and websockets for high-throughput streaming use cases.
[09:45] Tom: Anything to call out re: DLP integration? we need to ensure certain fields are redacted before leaving the org boundary.
[09:52] Samira: You can configure pre-send hooks in the SDK to call your DLP service. For Private deployments this can be enforced at the gateway or even in the sidecar. We'll share example middleware code.
[10:05] Maya: Example of request flow for RAG: 1) user query -> gateway (auth + tenant) -> retrieval service -> augment prompt -> call Redwood -> stream response back. We need to ensure the retrieval step doesn't leak PII.
[10:20] Diego: Right, make sure retrieval uses vector filters and PII scrubbing upstream. On the Redwood side we support masked request logging and pseudonymization options for request metadata.
[10:35] Evan: On the SDK side, is there a lightweight binary or do we use pure Python/Node packages? we prefer minimal footprint.
[10:43] Diego: It's pure Python and Node packages with optional native extensions for high-throughput batching. For extremely tight environments we can provide a thin REST shim.
[10:55] Rhiannon: For testing, can we run synthetic workloads? we'll want to simulate retrieval + 1.2s think-time and bursts.
[11:05] Samira: We can orchestrate a benchmark run with your traffic shape. Diego will own test harness and we'll need sample prompts and expected success criteria.
[11:15] Maya: Observability again — we'd like to tag requests with customer tenant and feature flags so we can split metrics by feature. any built-in metadata fields?
[11:25] Diego: You can attach up to N free-form tags per request (we can confirm exact limits), and we allow metadata blobs that show up in Console and logs. Best practice is to send a small JSON with tenant_id, feature_flag, correlation id.
[11:42] Tom: About policy and governance — do you support role-based access to model deployments, e.g. limit who can deploy a model variant to production?
[11:51] Samira: Yes; RBAC with teams and roles. For Dedicated and Private you can map to your SSO via SAML/SCIM and enforce approval gates for rollouts. We also have canary and A/B rollout controls.
[12:08] Evan: Let's surface a concrete plan. propose a pilot: Dedicated pool in eu-west-1, two weeks of benchmarks, SDK + LangChain connector integration, security review, and then decision to move to Private for high-sensitivity flows. timeline?
[12:21] Samira: Sounds good. timeline-wise: security review materials by 2028-05-10, SDK examples by 2028-05-09, pilot kickoff 2028-05-20, report 2028-06-03.
[12:33] Rhiannon: For the pilot, do you need sample data or can we anonymize?
[12:38] Diego: Anonymized samples are fine; real patterns are better for latency characteristics. If you can't share real data, synthetic data that matches token distribution works.
[12:50] Evan: Any other gotchas? cost controls, runaway jobs?
[12:54] Diego: We support soft and hard quota enforcement. You can set alerts on usage and automatic fallback to cheaper model families. Also, an emergency kill-switch can be configured at the tenant level.
[13:08] Tom: Who on Redwood will be our point for security/legal questions?
[13:12] Samira: I'll be primary AE contact; legal/security will be Diego for technical, and we'll loop in our compliance team if needed. I'll attach a security pack with the SOC2 report, encryption design, and data flow diagrams.
[13:27] Maya: Are there examples of customers who've migrated from hosted to Dedicated/Private? we want references for our compliance committee.
[13:35] Samira: Yes, we have a few case studies — we'll share references and a sanitized architecture doc.
[13:44] Evan: Great. Let's capture action items and next steps.

Recap and action items (verbatim):
[13:55] Samira: Action items: 1) send security docs (SOC2, KMS notes), 2) SDK + LangChain/LlamaIndex snippets, 3) customer to share traffic and sample prompts, 4) schedule pilot for week of May 20th.
[14:10] Maya: we'll get the sample prompts and traffic histogram by next week.
[14:18] Tom: I'll review the security pack and flag any must-haves.
[14:25] Samira: Diego will post the SDK examples and an OpenTelemetry exporter snippet.
[14:31] Diego: Yep. I'll include a sidecar example and a LangChain attribution wrapper with caching best-practices.
